33:22 When the teenage son said “cancer sucks” it hit home hard for me. I was 14 myself when my mom was diagnosed with stage 3A breast cancer, none of our extended family members would help us when she was fighting cancer (due to past family squabbles that they never even had the guts to talk to me about) so we were on our own. I wound up being her soul caretaker. The doctors initially thought that she would only live three more years, but she fought for a solid 10. She was also a charge nurse like Dana so she knew the odds of her survival better than most. And like Dr. Mike’s mom, my mom didn’t die from the cancer. She unfortunately caught Hepatitis C almost 20 years earlier from a contaminated blood transfusion during a spinal surgery, so after she had her chemotherapy and radiotherapy her white blood cell count was halved, combined that with the Hepatitis C and her white blood cell count was quartered. In the end, she passed away peacefully from liver failure. Which was honestly the best way she could’ve died because people that die from liver failure don’t experience any pain or suffering, they just lose energy, fall asleep, and then pass.

If you know anyone who has a family member who is fighting cancer, go to them, talk to them, even hug them if they’re all right with it. Cancer isn’t just a battle that the patient fights, but their loved ones fight as well.

comments.text: That whole "treat the patient, not the imaging/lab values" is interesting to hear, because I had a situation like that. For roughly 17 years, I had extremely weird menstruation. Like, I would bleed for weeks (sometimes months) on end, heavily, and sometimes I'd go months between periods and other times I'd be period-free for maybe a week before I started hemorrhaging again. To this day, I have no idea where my body was finding all that blood and tissue. I finally convinced a doctor to actually look into it after I bled heavily for five months straight. Apparently my iron levels were so catastrophically low that it was nothing short of a miracle that I was conscious, let alone functional in any capacity. She put me on heavy-duty iron supplements and some heavy-duty birth control in an effort to basically shut everything down so my body could recover. Told me a few months later that my iron levels were low enough that it would not have been an overreaction on her part to have me loaded up in the ambulance and shipped over to the nearest ER for emergency transfusions. The only reason she didn't is because I was alert (permanently exhausted but aware) and functioning relatively normally. It took over two years of daily heavy-duty iron supplements to finally push my iron levels back across the bottom end of the normal range.
